adjudicated.jp: 自宅に戻ると、足下にダンボール箱が置いてある。
adjudicated.en: On return to my home, I found a cardboard box set at my feet.

The countable contents require a determiner here: 'The contents were food.'

adjudicated.jp: 本当に一人一人に配送してるんだな。
adjudicated.en: He is really delivering them one by one.
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese emphasizes delivery to each individual person. The English pronoun can instead make the items themselves arrive singly.
The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "...really giving it all like Dek**ugi-kun, aren't you.
comments: http://doraemon.wikia.com/wiki/Hidetoshi_Dekisugi There's no asterisk, but it's still censored, as it plays the pun straight: 'dekisugi' means "to do too much", but where in Doraemon it's written with other kanji, here it's written with the straightforwards kanji for "do/be able to". -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The line's Dekisugi reference labels Tomoki an overachieving model child. The English paraphrase 'giving it all' does not preserve that function, adds a question tag, and fails to close the quotation mark.

adjudicated.jp: それほどまでに本気だということだ。
adjudicated.en: This is the level of seriousness this reaches,
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says this shows how serious Tomoki is. The English recursively makes seriousness reach a level and leaves the sentence open with a comma.
